symptom: U+0000-U+001F (except tab/LF/CR) are illegal in XML 1.0; Salesforce long-text can contain them.
seenIn: office-kit writes _x0001_ (correct); ExcelJS silently strips them; openpyxl raises IllegalCharacterError and refuses the cell; Excel decodes _x0001_ back to the control char.
expected: Writer: encode as _xHHHH_. Reader: decode _xHHHH_ to the character.

symptom: Literal text that looks like an escape (_x0041_) must be written as _x005F_x0041_ or readers decode it to 'A'.
seenIn: ExcelJS, SheetJS, write-excel-file, XlsxWriter write _x0041_ raw (read back as 'A'); office-kit escapes the first underscore correctly.
expected: Writer: prefix every _xHHHH_-shaped run with _x005F_. Reader: decode _x005F_ to '_' and continue scanning after it.

symptom: Overlapping escape-shaped runs: the literal _x005F_x0041_ needs three escapes (_x005F_x005F_x005F_x0041_).
seenIn: office-kit writes _x005F_x005F_x0041_, which Excel and SheetJS both decode to '_x005FA' (Excel oracle F3).
expected: Escape every underscore that starts an _xHHHH_ match, including the underscore shared by two matches.

symptom: _X0041_ (uppercase X) is not an escape per ST_Xstring; SheetJS decodes it to 'A' anyway.
seenIn: SheetJS reader (case-insensitive regex); office-kit reader leaves it as text.
expected: Only lowercase _x + 4 hex digits + _ is an escape.
status: SheetJS reader over-eager; Excel behaviour recorded in oracle F7

symptom: Reader returns the raw _x0001_ / _x000d_ text instead of the character.
seenIn: office-kit reader (document and stream) on SheetJS/office-kit output.
expected: Decode on read (Excel does).
status: office-kit reader bug (upstream issue; related to open issue #131 on numeric char refs)

symptom: A raw CR inside <t> is collapsed to LF by XML line-end normalization; Excel writes CR as _x000D_.
seenIn: ExcelJS, write-excel-file, openpyxl, XlsxWriter emit raw CR (lost by every reader); office-kit emits _x000D_ but SheetJS's unescapexml then collapses \r\n to \n on read.
expected: Writer: escape CR as _x000D_. Reader: decode it and do not normalize.

symptom: Leading/trailing/only-whitespace strings need xml:space="preserve" or some readers trim them.
seenIn: calamine trims a whitespace-only cell to '' (openpyxl golden). All JS writers emit the attribute.
expected: Emit xml:space="preserve" whenever the text starts/ends with whitespace.

symptom: Cells above 32,767 chars: SheetJS throws 'Text length must not exceed 32767 characters'; other writers emit an invalid file.
seenIn: Jetstream truncates with '...(truncated)' (prepareExcelFile); Permission Manager path does not.
expected: Truncate with a visible suffix and report the count (policy:truncate-32767).

symptom: Text starting with '=' ('=SUM(A1)', '=cmd|calc') becomes a formula; Excel then REPAIRS the file ('Removed Records: Formula').
seenIn: openpyxl (smart typing) and LibreOffice CSV import. SheetJS/ExcelJS/office-kit/XlsxWriter keep it as text.
expected: Never infer formulas from user text (formula-injection surface); write t="s"/inlineStr.

symptom: Workbook without xl/sharedStrings.xml, every string inline (t="inlineStr").
seenIn: SheetJS bookSST:false (Jetstream default); accepted by Excel, LibreOffice, calamine, openpyxl, office-kit.
expected: Readers must not require the SST part.

symptom: Excel displays/rounds to 15 significant digits: 9007199254740991 shows as 9.007199254741E+15.
seenIn: Excel oracle I2. Files may still carry 17 digits; readers return the stored double.
expected: Store shortest round-trip; document that Excel UI shows 15 digits.

symptom: 1.7976931348623157e308 round-trips as Infinity or is dropped.
seenIn: openpyxl reads its own output as inf; office-kit drops the cell (null) from openpyxl/XlsxWriter files.
expected: Parse xsd:double exactly; treat overflow as an error cell rather than dropping the cell.

symptom: -0 has no representation; readers return 0.
seenIn: all writers/readers
expected: Normalize -0 to 0.

symptom: Library computes the serial from a Date's UTC fields, so a local-midnight Date lands in the file with the host UTC offset as a time fraction (07:00 here); Excel shows 7:00 AM or ######## for negatives.
seenIn: office-kit dateToExcel/excelToDate ('wall clock in UTC fields' convention, like openpyxl naive datetimes). SheetJS write uses local fields; SheetJS raw read returns UTC-field Dates and sheet_to_json converts with utc_to_local.
expected: Document the convention and convert at the boundary: new Date(Date.UTC(y,m,d,h,i,s)) before handing local Dates to office-kit.
status: verified (Excel oracle M2/N2/O2 on the office-kit golden)

symptom: A time-only value carried as a JS Date on 1899-12-30 is written as a NEGATIVE serial; Excel shows ########.
seenIn: SheetJS datenum (res < 60 => res - 1) and office-kit dateToExcel both produce -0.47 for 1899-12-30T12:34:56.
expected: Represent time-only values as a fraction of a day (serial 0.x, Excel's 'Jan 0 1900').

symptom: Serial 60 is the fake 1900-02-29; serials 1-59 map to 1900-01-01..02-28 and 61+ to 03-01 onward.
seenIn: SheetJS returns the raw number 60 (no Date) for that cell; office-kit maps 60 to 02-28; XlsxWriter writes 1900-01-01 12:00 as serial 0.5 (Excel shows '1/0/1900 12:00').
expected: Map 60 to a documented value; never shift real dates.

symptom: Dates before 1900-01-01 are not representable as Excel dates (serial <= 0 shows '1/0/1900' or ########); Salesforce allows dates from 1700.
seenIn: All writers emit serial 0/negative for 1899-12-31.
expected: Write pre-1900 dates as text (ISO) or reject with a clear error.

symptom: Constructing a local Date for a wall clock that does not exist (US DST gap 02:30) silently shifts it by one hour before it reaches the file.
seenIn: Every JS writer fed local Dates (dst-gap-shift-1h in the diffs).
expected: Carry wall-clock components (or UTC-field Dates) instead of local Date instants.

symptom: JS Dates before ~1901 carry LMT offsets (e.g. -7:52:58 in Los Angeles), so UTC-field <-> local conversions of 1899/1900 dates are off by minutes/seconds.
seenIn: historical-tz-offset-shift category on 1900-01-01 12:00 values.
expected: Avoid local-time math for pre-1901 dates; use UTC fields.

symptom: A date cell is a number whose cellXf number format is a date format; readers that skip styles return raw serials.
seenIn: office-kit loadWorkbook and loadWorkbookStream both return serials; the consumer must resolve cellXfs -> numFmtId -> isDateFormat.
expected: Expose typed Dates or a one-call resolver; built-in ids 14-22/45-47 plus custom codes containing y/m/d/h/s outside quotes/brackets.

symptom: With cellText:false SheetJS error cells carry only the BIFF code in v (42 = #N/A) and no w text.
seenIn: Jetstream's read options.
expected: Map codes to error names (0 #NULL!, 7 #DIV/0!, 15 #VALUE!, 23 #REF!, 29 #NAME?, 36 #NUM!, 42 #N/A).

symptom: Writers without an error-cell API write '#N/A' as a string (t="s"), which readers cannot distinguish from an error.
seenIn: XlsxWriter (no write_error), write-excel-file.
expected: Use t="e" for errors.

symptom: Formula whose cached value is an error (=1/0) - some writers cannot express the cached error.
seenIn: office-kit setFormula cachedValue accepts number|string|boolean only; openpyxl never writes cached values.
expected: Writer supports t="e" + <f>; reader returns the cached value.

symptom: A missing <c> and an empty-string cell are different things; readers disagree on which they return.
seenIn: calamine returns '' for blanks (skip_empty_area=False); write-excel-file/XlsxWriter write '' as blank; Jetstream defval:'' maps both to ''.
expected: Define the contract (Jetstream: '' for both).

symptom: Rich text is <r> runs in SST/inline strings; readers must flatten.
seenIn: ExcelJS, office-kit ({ kind: 'rich-text', runs }), openpyxl, XlsxWriter write runs; SheetJS CE flattens on read.
expected: Flatten to plain text on read; writing runs is optional.

symptom: Time-only cells (serial < 1) come back as a datetime on 1899-12-31 (Excel's 'Jan 0 1900') or 1899-12-30 depending on the reader.
seenIn: SheetJS -> 1899-12-31; office-kit excelToDate -> 1899-12-31; openpyxl -> datetime.time when the format is a time format.
expected: Document the marker date; Jetstream's transformTime must accept both.

symptom: CT_Font children have a fixed schema order (b, i, strike, ..., sz, color, name, family, charset, scheme); most writers emit them out of order.
seenIn: Open XML SDK validator fails ExcelJS ('sz' unexpected), office-kit ('b', 'color'), write-excel-file ('b'), openpyxl ('color'). Excel and LibreOffice open them anyway.
expected: Emit in schema order so strict validators pass.

symptom: <col width> above 255 violates the schema.
seenIn: LibreOffice CSV import writes width 296.22 for the 40,000-char column; validator FAIL, Excel opens it.
expected: Clamp widths to 255.

symptom: Streaming writers set general-purpose bit 3 and put sizes/CRC in a trailing data descriptor.
seenIn: Google Sheets export (the shipped multi-object template), ExcelJS streaming, office-kit streaming.
expected: Readers must honour bit 3 (read sizes from the central directory); Excel accepts it.

symptom: [Content_Types].xml is the last zip entry, not the first.
seenIn: Google Sheets export.
expected: Locate parts via the central directory, never by entry order.

symptom: Extra parts without extensions (xl/metadata, xl/commentsmeta0) and legacy VML comment parts.
seenIn: Google Sheets export.
expected: Ignore unknown parts; resolve everything through rels + content types.

symptom: Legacy notes are stored as xl/commentsN.xml plus VML drawings.
seenIn: Google Sheets export, ExcelJS, office-kit, openpyxl, XlsxWriter, SheetJS.
expected: Readers may ignore; writers that emit notes must emit both parts.

symptom: Multi-object loader skips any sheet whose lowercased name contains 'instructions'.
seenIn: Jetstream load-records-multi-object-utils.ts; shipped template has an 'Instructions' sheet.
expected: Preserve this rule in any replacement.

symptom: B1 object, B2 operation, B3 external id, row 5 headers, data from row 6; sparse cell access by A1 address.
seenIn: Jetstream multi-object loader.
expected: Reader exposes cheap A1 access for a prefix region plus a row-range/array mode.

symptom: CSV bytes reach the xlsx parser (Electron open-with, Google Drive alt=media).
seenIn: Jetstream parseFile; SheetJS sniffs and parses CSV silently.
expected: Sniff magic bytes and route text to papaparse.

symptom: CSV imported by a spreadsheet app re-types every column (leading zeros lost, '=text' evaluated, dates guessed).
seenIn: LibreOffice CSV import golden (Excel repaired it because of the evaluated formulas).
expected: Treat CSV-derived workbooks as untyped; expect surprises in the first row.

symptom: Writer refuses the whole cell when it contains a control character.
seenIn: openpyxl IllegalCharacterError.
expected: Escape instead of rejecting.

symptom: 31-char sheet name with an apostrophe inside; formulas referencing it need quoting.
seenIn: Every generator wrote it; every reader read it back.
expected: Allow; reject only : \ / ? * [ ] and leading/trailing apostrophes.

symptom: Hand-built minimal 7-part workbook (content types, rels, workbook, styles, SST, one sheet).
seenIn: Opened by every reader, Excel, LibreOffice; validator PASS.
expected: Reference point for the other edge fixtures.

symptom: Worksheet without <dimension> (Google Sheets omits it).
seenIn: All readers derive the range from the cells.
expected: Never require <dimension>.

symptom: <row> and <c> without r attributes: positions must be inferred (previous row/col + 1).
seenIn: SheetJS, calamine, LibreOffice and Excel infer them; office-kit loadWorkbook throws 'worksheet: <row> missing required @r' and loadWorkbookStream returns every cell at the wrong position (0/9); openpyxl handles it.
expected: Infer positions.

symptom: <v/> (empty value) and <c s="1"/> (no value child) must read as blank.
seenIn: SheetJS/office-kit/openpyxl blank; calamine returns '' for <v/> and treats the styled empty cell differently (type-mismatch / date-as-text).
expected: Blank, never 0 or ''.

symptom: CDATA sections and rich-text runs inside <is>.
seenIn: Every reader flattened them identically.
expected: Support CDATA and <r> runs in inline strings.

symptom: Worksheet XML with a namespace prefix on every element (<x:sheetData>).
seenIn: All readers, LibreOffice and Excel fine; the Open XML SDK validator FAILS it.
expected: Match element local names, not prefixed names.

symptom: Strict OOXML (purl.oclc.org namespaces, Strict relationship types, t="d" ISO date cells).
seenIn: SheetJS, LibreOffice and Excel open it; office-kit fails ('root rels missing officeDocument relationship'), calamine 'Relationship not found', openpyxl finds no sheet.
expected: Match relationship types by suffix and accept both namespace families.

symptom: Relationship targets written as absolute part names (/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml).
seenIn: All readers handle it.
expected: Resolve absolute and relative targets.

symptom: Relationship target with a Windows separator (worksheets\sheet1.xml).
seenIn: SheetJS, LibreOffice and Excel open it; office-kit 'sheet part not found', calamine WorksheetNotFound, openpyxl no sheet.
expected: Normalize backslashes to slashes.
status: office-kit reader gap (calamine changelog 0.29 fixed the same)

symptom: Entries stored uncompressed (method 0).
seenIn: All readers fine.
expected: Support stored and deflated entries.

symptom: t="s" cell whose index exceeds the shared string table.
seenIn: SheetJS throws, office-kit loadWorkbook throws a clear error, loadWorkbookStream silently drops the cells, openpyxl/calamine throw; Excel opens the file (no recovery log).
expected: Treat as blank with a warning, matching Excel.

symptom: workbookPr date1904="1" shifts the epoch by 1,462 days.
seenIn: office-kit handles it; SheetJS raw cells, openpyxl and calamine returned the 1900-epoch date in this run (to re-check via sheet_to_json).
expected: Honour date1904 everywhere dates are decoded.

symptom: state="hidden" and state="veryHidden" worksheets.
seenIn: All readers list them; Jetstream's picker shows every sheet name today.
expected: Expose the state so the UI can hide or mark them.

symptom: DOCTYPE with external and recursive entities in sharedStrings.xml.
seenIn: office-kit rejects ('DTD declarations are not permitted'); openpyxl/calamine reject undefined entities; SheetJS accepts and leaves '&xxe;' as literal text (no expansion, no rejection).
expected: Reject DOCTYPE outright.

symptom: Archive cut before the central directory.
seenIn: Every reader rejects (SheetJS 'Bad compressed size', office-kit 'no End-of-Central-Directory signature').
expected: Clear error.

symptom: Entry CRC does not match the data.
seenIn: SheetJS and office-kit accept (no CRC check); openpyxl and calamine reject; validator PASS.
expected: Either is defensible; document it.

symptom: Two entries named xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml.
seenIn: SheetJS uses the FIRST entry (3 rows); office-kit, openpyxl and calamine use the LAST (1 row).
expected: Reject, or pick deterministically and warn.

symptom: 50,000 nested <r> runs in one shared string.
seenIn: Every reader rejects (office-kit 'Maximum nested tags exceeded'); the Open XML SDK validator crashes with a stack overflow.
expected: Depth cap with a clear error.

symptom: 30 MB sheet XML deflated ~190:1.
seenIn: SheetJS parses it fully; office-kit has decompression limits (see hostile run).
expected: Cap inflated bytes and ratio; fail fast.

symptom: .ods bytes with an .xlsx name.
seenIn: SheetJS parses ODS silently (Jetstream today); office-kit 'missing [Content_Types].xml', openpyxl KeyError, calamine '_rels/.rels not found'.
expected: Detect the mimetype entry and say 'OpenDocument file - save as .xlsx'.

symptom: BIFF8 .xls bytes with an .xlsx name (CFB container).
seenIn: SheetJS parses BIFF8 silently; office-kit reports 'Encrypted xlsx is not supported' (misclassifies any CFB file as encrypted); calamine 'invalid Zip archive' when the extension says xlsx.
expected: Distinguish legacy .xls (Workbook stream) from encrypted (EncryptedPackage stream) and say which.

symptom: Password-protected workbook (CFB with EncryptedPackage).
seenIn: office-kit: 'Encrypted xlsx is not supported. Decrypt with msoffcrypto-tool first.' (does not contain 'password-protected', which Jetstream's UI matches on); calamine 'Workbook is password protected'; SheetJS throws.
expected: Error whose message includes 'password-protected' (or an adapter mapping).

symptom: SpreadsheetML 2003 XML text with an .xlsx name.
seenIn: Every reader rejects with a zip error; SheetJS rejects too.
expected: Sniff and say 'not an xlsx'.

symptom: 1900-02-28 written as serial 60 (Excel shows 1900-02-29 / Mar 1).
seenIn: SheetJS (datenum uses < 60 instead of < 61), write-excel-file, LibreOffice CSV import; ExcelJS shifts every pre-1900-03-01 date by +1 day and +UTC offset.
expected: Serial 59 for 1900-02-28; only serials >= 61 skip the fake day.

symptom: 1900-01-01 12:00 written as serial 0.5 (Excel value 1899-12-31 12:00).
seenIn: XlsxWriter 3.2.9 golden (Excel oracle O6); openpyxl writes 1.5 correctly.
expected: Serial 1.5.
status: observed (verify against XlsxWriter's documented epoch handling)

symptom: Excel's displayed text shows ######## when the column is too narrow, and AppleScript date values pass through macOS local-time normalization (02:30 in a DST gap reads as 03:30).
seenIn: Excel oracle sentinel table.
expected: Read `value` for numbers/dates and widen columns in goldens; treat DST-gap displays as oracle noise.

symptom: Custom date/time number formats (yyyy-mm-dd, hh:mm:ss, yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss) import into Google Sheets with no named format selected in Format > Number.
seenIn: User check of the ExcelJS golden in Google Sheets (2026-09-12); the re-export is fixture golden-canonical-gsheets-resave.
expected: Values stay dates; verify what numFmt Google writes back on export.

symptom: A list data validation ('Red,Green,Blue') imports into Google Sheets as a rule ('Input must be an item on the specified list') without the dropdown chip.
seenIn: User check of the ExcelJS golden in Google Sheets.
expected: Load-template picklists would need Google's own dropdown format; note for the v2 data-validation feature.

symptom: Numbers replaces formulas it does not support with their cached value on import ('Unsupported formulas were replaced by the last calculated value').
seenIn: Numbers 14.4 importing the ExcelJS golden (=NA(), =1/0, =Data!A2&"x").
expected: Cached values must be present in written files or Numbers users see blanks.

symptom: Numbers makes hidden sheets visible on import ('Hidden sheets were made visible: Sheet: Hidden') and its export loses the hidden state.
seenIn: Numbers 14.4 importing the ExcelJS golden.
expected: Do not rely on hidden sheets to hide data from users.

symptom: Salesforce 'Details Only' report export: Apache POI workbook, one sheet, header row first, typed cells (dates, currency, percent, booleans).
seenIn: golden-sfdc-report-details (dev org, 2026-09-12).
expected: Load Records must map its header row and typed values like any other upload.

symptom: Salesforce 'Formatted Report' export: report title and filter rows above the header, grouping/subtotal and footer rows below, merged cells.
seenIn: golden-sfdc-report-formatted.
expected: Header detection must skip the title block; footer rows must not become records.

symptom: Files whose first row is not the header (report titles) and whose last rows are totals.
seenIn: Salesforce Formatted Report export; common in exports from BI tools.
expected: Offer a header-row picker or heuristics; today parseWorkbook treats row 1 as the header.

symptom: Apache POI writes xsd:boolean attributes as true/false (customWidth="true") where Excel writes 1/0.
seenIn: Salesforce report exports.
expected: Accept true/false/1/0 for every boolean attribute.

symptom: Excel's CSV import re-types every column (leading zeros dropped, =text evaluated or quoted, dates parsed with locale rules, 17-digit integers rounded to 15 digits).
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-from-csv, golden-canonical-gsheets-from-csv.
expected: Compare with the reader dumps to document what survives; explains why users' CSV-derived uploads differ from the source system.

symptom: Apache POI writes <u val="none"/> in fonts; 'none' is a legal ST_UnderlineValues member but office-kit's parser only accepts single/double/singleAccounting/doubleAccounting and throws.
seenIn: Both Salesforce report exports (golden-sfdc-report-details/-formatted): office-kit loadWorkbook and loadWorkbookStream fail; SheetJS, openpyxl, calamine, LibreOffice and Excel open them.
expected: Accept every ST_UnderlineValues member, and generally never fail a whole workbook on a style enum.
status: office-kit reader bug - BLOCKING for Jetstream (users upload Salesforce report exports)

symptom: Apache POI writes 6-digit colour values (rgb="8E9297") where the schema requires 8-digit ARGB hexBinary.
seenIn: Salesforce report exports: 20 and 39 validator errors; Excel and every reader tolerate it.
expected: Accept 6- and 8-digit hex on read; write 8-digit ARGB.

symptom: Excel opens a UTF-8 CSV without a byte-order mark using the legacy code page: 'Zoë Ångström' becomes 'Zo√´ √Öngstr√∂m', Hebrew becomes box characters.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-from-csv (Excel 365 macOS opening canonical.csv). Jetstream's prepareCsvFile (papaparse unparse) writes no BOM; the docs warn Windows users to use the UTF-8 import option.
expected: Prefix CSV exports with \uFEFF (hardening candidate, 08) or steer users to xlsx.

symptom: Excel's CSV import evaluates '=SUM(A1)' as a formula (cached 0) - the classic CSV injection path.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-from-csv G2 read back as a formula cell.
expected: CSV exports of user data need the same '=text' hygiene as xlsx (quote or prefix); another reason to prefer xlsx.

symptom: Excel's CSV import kept 16-17 digit integers as text and ISO dates such as 1899-12-31 / 2024-03-10T02:30:00.000 as text, while typing 12:34:56.789 as a time.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-from-csv (number-as-text 36, date-as-text 32, time typed).
expected: Document; CSV-derived uploads carry Excel's heuristics, not the source types.

symptom: LibreOffice's CSV import drops leading zeros ('00123' -> 123), keeps TRUE/FALSE as text and ISO dates as text, and evaluates '=text' as formulas.
seenIn: golden-canonical-libreoffice-from-csv vs expected/canonical-csv-import.json (text-as-number 42, boolean-as-text 30, date-as-text 30).
expected: Document; CSV-derived uploads differ per importing application.

symptom: Excel's Strict Open XML save writes t="d" cells as ISO strings with 17 fractional digits (2024-03-10T09:29:59.9999995809048412) and time-only cells as bare times (19:34:56.789…); the Open XML SDK validator rejects them (133 errors, incl. 0%/800% attribute values in drawing fallbacks).
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-strict (Excel 365 macOS 16.03).
expected: Readers must parse ISO 8601 with arbitrary fraction digits and bare times; do not trust the validator for Strict files.

symptom: A genuine Excel 'Strict Open XML Spreadsheet' file cannot be opened by office-kit ('root rels missing officeDocument relationship'), calamine ('Relationship not found') or openpyxl (no sheets); SheetJS, LibreOffice and Excel open it.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-strict.
expected: Match relationship types by suffix; accept purl.oclc.org namespaces.
status: verified (upgrades EC-STRICT-NAMESPACES from hand-built to real-world)

symptom: Numbers exports the max double as <v>inf</v>; openpyxl crashes (int('inf')) and Excel repairs the sheet ('Repaired Records: Cell information from /xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml part').
seenIn: golden-canonical-numbers (Numbers 14.4 export of the ExcelJS golden).
expected: Never emit inf/nan; readers should treat non-numeric <v> in a numeric cell as an error cell rather than crash.

symptom: Excel re-saving a library-written workbook preserves the library's serials exactly (ExcelJS's +7h UTC shift, office-kit's negative time serials), so a bad writer's dates cannot be 'fixed' by an Excel round trip.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-resave (M2 = 1.2916666666678793) and -resave-office-kit.
expected: Fix dates at write time.

symptom: Google Sheets' CSV import trims leading/trailing whitespace, drops leading zeros ('00123' -> 123), keeps 17-digit integers as text, names the sheet after the file including the extension ('canonical.csv'), and evaluates '=SUM(A1)' / '=cmd|calc' as formulas - Excel then repairs the exported file ('Removed Records: Formula').
seenIn: golden-canonical-gsheets-from-csv (2026-09-12 redo): whitespace-trimmed 12, text-as-number 38, number-as-text 16; Excel oracle REPAIRED.
expected: Same as the other CSV importers: treat CSV-derived uploads as re-typed; '=text' is a formula-injection surface in every spreadsheet app.

symptom: Single-sheet workbooks produced from a CSV carry the file name as the sheet name ('canonical' in Excel/LibreOffice, 'canonical.csv' in Google Sheets).
seenIn: All three CSV-import goldens.
expected: Never assume 'Sheet1'; the oracle compares single-sheet workbooks by position.

symptom: On a workbook saved with the 1904 date system, SheetJS's raw cells (cellDates:true, before sheet_to_json) come back 1,462 days early; office-kit, openpyxl and calamine apply the epoch.
seenIn: golden-canonical-excel-365-1904 (Excel 365 re-save with date1904=1): sheetjs temporal-mismatch 90 vs office-kit 65 (its usual UTC-field shift only).
expected: Honour workbookPr date1904 wherever serials are decoded; Jetstream reads through sheet_to_json, which must be checked separately.

symptom: Excel 16 for Mac's AppleScript 'workbook normal file format' saves the default format (xlsx), not Excel 97-2004; BIFF8 is 'Excel98to2004 file format' and xlsb is 'Excel binary file format'. There is no Strict Open XML member and no ad-hoc VBA hook.
seenIn: fixtures/generators/excel-goldens.mjs (2026-09-12).
expected: Use the Excel98to2004 / Excel binary enumerators for legacy sources; save Strict by hand.

symptom: .xlsb (Excel Binary Workbook) bytes under an .xlsx name: a zip whose parts are binary records (xl/workbook.bin, sheet1.bin), so it passes a zip-signature sniff but has no SpreadsheetML.
seenIn: hostile-xlsb-renamed (Excel 365 'Excel binary file format' save).
expected: Detect via [Content_Types].xml (application/vnd.ms-excel.sheet.binary.macroEnabled.main) and say 'save as .xlsx'.
